faqs.q: What is a RAG chatbot?
faqs.a: A RAG chatbot looks up the right passages in your own documents first and only then writes its answer from them. RAG stands for retrieval-augmented generation. Because the answer is built from your documents, it can show its source. It can also say "not found" when the documents do not cover the question, instead of guessing.

faqs.q: How do you stop a chatbot from making things up?
faqs.a: With several layers, not one instruction. First the chatbot checks that the documents really contain the answer. Weak matches never reach the AI language model (LLM), the part that writes the reply. A fixed fallback sentence covers the rest. In my healthcare example, out-of-scope questions get a plain "not found" instead of a guess.

faqs.q: Can a chatbot run on my own servers?
faqs.a: Often, yes. At work I build on AI models hosted on the client's own servers, so no data or prompts leave the building. My personal projects use online services such as Groq. During planning we choose what fits your privacy needs, budget and answer quality.

faqs.q: How much does an AI chatbot cost for a website?
faqs.a: I do not publish a price list, because chatbots vary a lot. The cost depends on how many documents you have, how they are organised, where the chatbot must run and how much testing you need. After reading your brief I suggest a fixed price or hourly billing. We agree it in writing before I start.

faqs.q: What kinds of documents can the chatbot use?
faqs.a: Text-based documents such as policies, manuals, circulars and support articles. Tables and images inside documents can be harder, so we test those early. I start with a small sample of yours to check how well the chatbot finds the right passages, before we commit to the full build.

faqs.q: Can my team maintain it after you finish?
faqs.a: That is the aim. Instructions and adjustable settings live in simple settings files, and the code has tests. The handover includes a walkthrough of how to add documents and tune the settings. If you want ongoing help, we can agree a maintenance period in writing.

faqs.a: Document AI is software that reads documents such as PDFs, forms and reports. It turns what they say into structured data you can search, check and use. It can pull out names, dates, amounts and obligations. I build it so every extracted fact links back to the exact quote in the source document.

faqs.q: Is FastAPI used in production?

faqs.q: Which is better, FastAPI or Django?
faqs.a: FastAPI suits services built around an API, including AI features. Django with Django REST Framework suits products that also need an admin area, user accounts and a built-in database layer. I use both and will recommend one after reading your requirements.

faqs.q: What is YOLO object detection?
faqs.a: YOLO, short for You Only Look Once, is a fast method that finds and labels many objects in an image or video frame. It works in one pass and draws a box around each. I have used the YOLOv8 version for detection. It suits live counting and alerts, though accuracy still has to be tested on your own footage.

faqs.q: How accurate is computer vision?
faqs.a: I will not promise a number before I see your data. I measure on data the model has not seen and state exactly how it was split. My deepfake detector reports 74.16% on a random frame-level split, and says what that does not prove.

faqs.q: How much does a computer vision project cost?
faqs.a: It depends on how much footage or how many images you have, how much labelling is needed. The accuracy you need and whether it must run live also matter. I do not publish a price list. faqs.q: Can you train a model on my own images or video?
faqs.a: Yes, for small to medium sets of images. I trained a neural network on frames from a public deepfake dataset. I have also used ready-made detectors such as Faster R-CNN, YOLOv8n and a Vision Transformer. During planning we check how much labelled data you have and whether a ready-made model is the better start.

faqs.q: Can it work on live camera feeds?
faqs.a: My monitoring prototype checks video frames on a schedule, one every three seconds for the crime module, and raises alerts. faqs.a: Those projects need consent, clear rules on how long data is kept and legal review on your side. I raise privacy questions during planning and can build in options such as limited data retention and restricted access to stored images. The legal decisions stay with you.

faq.q: How accurate is speech emotion recognition?
faq.a: In this project, 93.87% on a random 20% test split. That figure does not cover new speakers, because altered copies of one clip can land on both sides of the split. Accuracy on unseen voices will be lower, so a client project would first measure it by splitting speakers apart.

faq.q: Can it work with my own recordings?
faq.a: It can be retrained on your recordings if they are labelled with the emotions you care about. Quality depends on the microphone, the language and the number of speakers. I would first test it on a sample of your audio and tell you honestly how well it holds.

items.q: Can I hire an AI engineer who also has a full-time job?
items.a: Yes. I work as an AI Engineer at Claptek Pvt Ltd and take select freelance AI and backend projects alongside that job. I keep the number of clients small so each project gets proper attention. I am upfront about scope and timelines before we agree to work together.

items.q: Do you take on freelance projects?
items.a: Yes, a small number at a time. To start, send a short brief through the contact form or by email. I reply with any questions and a first view of scope and timeline. Nothing is built until we agree the plan in writing. I work remotely from Mumbai.

items.q: What kinds of projects do you build?
items.a: I build AI chatbots that answer from your documents, tools that read and extract data from documents, and Python backend APIs. I also build computer vision, speech and text models, and automation such as web scrapers and Telegram or WhatsApp bots. Each area has its own page under Services, with examples of real work.

items.q: What should I include in a project brief for an AI developer?
items.a: Say what you want to build and what a good result looks like, and roughly when you need it. Tell me anything I should know, such as private data, tools you already use or where it will run. Also say what you have already tried. A few lines are enough to start, and I ask for details later.

Send a short brief through the contact form or by email, as a few lines or a longer note. I read it, then reply with my view on feasibility and a proposed scope. We agree on both before I write any code.

items.q: Can you fix an existing AI project?
items.a: Yes. Most of my professional work has been inside software that already existed. I added an AI drafting service to a live audit product and sped up the core matching code during an internship. I read the code before changing it, keep changes tested and leave notes explaining each decision.

I work mostly in Python. For web services I use FastAPI and PostgreSQL, packaged with Docker (so it runs the same on any server). For AI I use services such as Groq and OpenAI, plus LangChain and ChromaDB for document chatbots. For vision and speech I use OpenCV, PyTorch and TensorFlow. The full list is on the About page.

items.q: Can the AI run on our own servers instead of an online service?
items.a: Yes. At work I build on AI language models (LLMs) hosted on the client's own servers. This suits systems where no data, prompt or usage record may leave the building. My personal projects use online services such as Groq. We choose based on your privacy needs, cost and answer quality.

items.q: Can a freelancer sign an NDA?
items.a: Yes. I am happy to sign a reasonable mutual NDA (a confidentiality agreement) before we discuss private details. I do not reuse client data or code in other projects. I only name a client or show their work in my portfolio with written approval.

items.q: Who owns the code written by a freelancer?
items.a: The ownership and licence terms are written into our agreement before work begins. The usual arrangement is that you own what you pay for. My freelance work is kept separate from my full-time job and never uses my employer's code or data.

items.q: What does a project look like from start to finish?
items.a: Four steps. First we agree on the problem and how success will be measured. Then I build a small working prototype on your data. Next I add tests and safety checks. Finally I hand over notes and a walkthrough. You see working software early and get short written updates along the way.

items.q: What time zone does a Mumbai freelance AI developer work in?
items.a: I am based in Mumbai, India, and work in Indian Standard Time (IST, UTC+5:30). I work remotely, using written updates and shared code reviews. We can agree meeting times that overlap with your working day. A past remote internship taught me how to keep distant teams in sync.

items.q: How much does it cost to hire an AI developer in India?
items.a: I do not publish a price list, because projects vary too much. After reading your brief, I suggest either a fixed price for a clearly defined scope, or hourly billing for open-ended work. The price and the terms are agreed in writing before I start.

items.q: How long does a freelance AI project take?
items.a: It depends on the size of the project. After reading your brief, I give a written estimate for each step. A small prototype is much quicker than a full product. I would rather give you an honest range than promise a date I cannot keep.

items.q: What happens after you hand the project over?
items.a: Handover includes a README (a how-to guide), setup instructions, tests and a walkthrough, so your team can run and extend the work. A bug-fix period and ongoing maintenance can be agreed as part of the scope, and I will write down exactly what is covered.
